statements.context: US House Energy and Commerce Committee hearing on data privacy shortfalls, focusing on AI chatbot interactions with teens.

statements.text: The October 7th export controls that the Biden Administration adopted to restrict the sale of advanced AI chips and advanced chipmaking equipment to China, I believe, was one of the two most important decisions the Biden Administration made in foreign policy last year. [...] we are actually degrading our own ability to enforce these export controls and to assess where export control restrictions would have our intended consequences, and I think that is a grave error on the part of the U.S. Government.
statements.context: Witness testimony at a U.S. congressional hearing on advanced technology threats to national security.

statements.text: AI right now is not inherently safe, but it is also not inherently dangerous. It will depend upon the work that we do in the coming years.
statements.context: Senate hearing on advanced technology and national-security threats, where a former government AI official discusses regulatory gaps in biosecurity and AI talent shortages.

statements.text: If the U.S. Government were, for example, to require that the makers of this type of software embed characteristics in the media files that allow them under technical analysis to be revealed as AI enabled forgeries, this would raise the cost and complexity of executing these types of forged media political interventions.
statements.context: Witness testimony before a congressional hearing on advanced technology and national-security threats.

statements.text: More than anything, we should use this opportunity to reinforce how important it is for the United States to have a national privacy standard.
statements.context: Opening remarks by Rep. Rick Allen at a House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee hearing on AI and data, followed by a question to a witness.

statements.text: A key issue associated with generative AI systems is the risk they pose for proliferating harmful content, including fake news, misinformation, disinformation, and entrenching bias against conservatives.
statements.context: Remarks by Rep. Rick Allen during a House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee hearing on artificial intelligence.

statements.text: Ms. Kak, should transparency about publishers' content in training datasets be part of the conversation about ethical AI?
statements.context: Question posed during a House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee hearing on AI and data innovation.

statements.text: H.R. 8939. A bill to amend the Communications Act of 1934 to establish technical and procedural standards for artificial or prerecorded voice systems created through generative artificial intelligence, and for other purposes; to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.
statements.context: Procedural reading of newly introduced public bills and resolutions in the House of Representatives.

statements.text: Mr. Shea, I have got 20 seconds. How can we use AI to secure our communications infrastructure from malicious actors?
statements.context: Brief question posed during a hearing titled 'AI in the Everyday: Current Applications and Future Frontiers in Communications and Technology'.
